messages:
maria: Heads up — since yesterday's IdP cert rotation we've seen a handful of users get duplicated accounts via SCIM (and some then enter a deprov loop). Happening ~1-2/min for certain bursts.
devon: ugh. can you paste a sample SCIM request/response and the okta provisioning log line?
maria: here's the SCIM server log snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-18T22:11:02Z INFO POST /scim/v2/Users 201 user created externalId: "okta|u-1234" -> local id: "u-789"
2026-03-18T22:11:02Z WARN retrying PATCH /scim/v2/Users/u-789 409 conflict: resourceVersion mismatch
2026-03-18T22:11:03Z INFO POST /scim/v2/Users 201 user created externalId: "okta|u-1234" -> local id: "u-790"
2026-03-18T22:11:03Z ERROR deprovision task failed: unable to find user with externalId "okta|u-1234"
```
aj: That pattern screams a timing/race during provisioning + our idempotency/key normalization blowing up. Two creates for same externalId in quick succession. Did we change how we compute externalId or strip session cookies after cert rotation?
simon: Not that I'm aware of. The cert rotation changed the SAML assertion encryption key (KMS alias rotated) and we rolled the service binary at the same time. Possible transient decrypt failures. okta-bot: PROVISIONING_EVENT user activate u-1234 -> SCIM request queued (req_id=rr-53).
maria: I also grabbed the Okta provisioning audit entry: `2026-03-18T22:11:02Z PROVISION user push to SCIM rr-53 status=200` but then `2026-03-18T22:11:03Z PROVISION user push to SCIM rr-54 status=201` (two pushes for same id).
devon: two pushes implies Okta retried because our endpoint returned a 5xx or took too long. Do we have high-latency traces?
aj: checked traces: our SCIM service saw a spike of KV cache misses around 22:11:02 (S3-backed user-metadata fetch) and one decrypt error from KMS: `InvalidCiphertextException` — but decrypt succeeded on retry. Looks like first request failed mid-path and Okta retried creating user resulting in duplicate because our create path doesn't enforce externalId uniqueness strictly enough in the short window.
maria: so root cause: KMS decrypt transient causing 5xx -> Okta retry -> duplicate create. Also our create path assigns a new local id before checking uniqueness/locking.
devon: quick mitigation: 1) pause auto-provisioning on Okta org (disable push) 2) enable a soft-guard on SCIM create to reject duplicate externalId within N seconds (return 200 if duplicate found) 3) roll back KMS alias change if still unstable.
simon: +1 on pause. We should also add a backfill/cleanup that consolidates duplicates and maps externalId to canonical local id.
aj: For longer term: add DB-level unique index on external_id with conditional upsert semantics (use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE RETURNING id`) and make the SCIM create idempotent by keying on `externalId`. Also add metrics: `scim.duplicates.count`, `scim.kms.decrypt_errors`.
maria: I've run a quick script to identify suspected duplicates: `SELECT external_id, array_agg(local_id) FROM users WHERE external_id LIKE 'okta|%' GROUP BY external_id HAVING count(*) > 1;` — output attached to ticket.
devon: action items: maria disable-okta-provisioning (owner maria), simon run cleanup script (owner simon), aj implement idempotent upsert patch (owner aj), infra to monitor KMS errors and revert alias if more InvalidCiphertextException spikes (owner devon).
simon: cleanup plan: 1) pick canonical local_id by last_login not null, 2) update references (rbac grants, session tokens) to canonical id, 3) drop duplicates, 4) emit audit log for each migrated ref — will do in a maintenance window.
maria: small gotcha — our audit pipeline currently drops fields on migration; make sure we include old_local_id and new_local_id in audit so compliance team can reconcile.
aj: ack. I'll add `migration_metadata` to the audit event schema.
okta-bot: ALERT: provisioning paused by maria at 22:28 UTC.
devon: after pause and quick rollback of the KMS alias we saw duplicate rate drop to 0 in the last 20m. But we still need the idempotent upsert and DB index.
maria: one more question — should we also log KMS key_id with every SAML decrypt attempt so we can trace which key produced transient failures?
aj: yes please. Add `kms_key_id` and `kms_request_id` to audit logs for decrypt attempt. That will help tie InvalidCiphertextException spikes to recent alias rotations.
simon: also propose a small change to Okta mapping: set `externalId` to `okta:{org}:{userId}` canonical form (we currently use `okta|userId`), normalize on ingest to avoid delimiter collisions when other idps are added.
maria: agreed. Let's file a follow-up RFC for canonical external_id format + migration plan.
devon: final note — we should notify compliance about the user dedupe and audit log plan. I'll loop them in.
maria: thanks all — I'll keep this thread updated with cleanup progress. :handshake:
